figures.alt: A casta painting of a Spanish man, an Indigenous woman, and their child in a cloth shop, labeled 'De español e india, mestiza' at the top.
figures.caption: Casta painting labeled 'De español e india, mestiza' (From a Spaniard and an Indigenous woman, a mestiza child), 18th century.

books.section: Topic 1.5 Labor, Slavery, and Caste in the Spanish Colonial System
The Social Structure of Spanish America
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.misconception: Denies mixing the painting itself shows.
options.text: Spaniards and Native peoples never mixed or formed families.

options.misconception: Claims artists refused to paint what this painting depicts.
options.text: Colonial artists refused to depict mixed-ancestry families in their work.
The colonial regime carefully classified people according to their ancestry.

options.misconception: Turns a ranking system into equal treatment.
options.text: The casta system treated every child identically regardless of parentage.

rationales.A: The painting itself depicts a mixed family, so mixing clearly occurred. The label names the child's mixed ancestry.
rationales.B: Casta paintings are precisely depictions of mixed families. The whole genre exists to show them.
rationales.C: Casta paintings exist because colonial society was organized around ancestry: each combination of parents produced a named category with legal and social consequences. Painting and labeling a 'mestiza' child shows how seriously the regime took classifying people by descent.
rationales.D: The whole point of the casta system was to treat people differently by ancestry. Identical treatment contradicts the labels.
rationales.general:
1. Read the label like a filing tag. It names the parents' origins and the child's category, mestiza.
2. Ask why a label exists. Labels exist because the regime sorted people by ancestry.
3. Ask what the painting shows. A mixed family, painted and named, proves mixing happened and was classified.
4. Rule out the rest. Mixing occurred, artists depicted it, and treatment differed by category.
Remember: when a source labels people by ancestry, ask what the labels were for: rank, not description.

stimulus.text: This 18th-century casta painting is labeled 'De español e india, mestiza' — 'From a Spaniard and an Indigenous woman, a mestiza child.' It shows a Spanish man, an Indigenous woman, and their child in a shop selling woven cloth.
